request.raw: Use FinRunbook to trace capital expenditure by Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta from 2023 onward. Map their relationships with suppliers of GPUs, semiconductor manufacturing, memory, networking, power, and cooling. Select no more than eight key suppliers and compare relevant revenue, orders, and profitability trends. Support every customer–supplier relationship with evidence. Do not add revenue across supply-chain layers and present the total as end-market size.
request.subject: AI infrastructure capital expenditure and supplier exposure: Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta
source_constraints: Primary company filings, earnings materials, and official releases first; secondary sources only for discovery or where the issuer does not name the counterparty.
assumptions: Capital expenditure is traced using each issuer reported cash purchases/additions of property and equipment; fiscal-year boundaries remain issuer-specific.
Latest interim data are included when publicly available as of 2026-09-03; estimates and guidance remain separate from actuals.
Valuation is omitted because the requested decision use concerns operating exposure and supply-chain transmission rather than security price.

selected_skills.name: sector-overview
selected_skills.purpose: Lead analytical structure for the AI-infrastructure value chain, supplier comparison, and investment implications.
selected_skills.expected_output: Layer-aware sector map and ranked supplier financial panel.

selected_skills.name: sec-10k-analysis
selected_skills.purpose: Extract and verify reported capex, revenue, operating profit, and supplier/customer disclosures from issuer filings.
selected_skills.expected_output: Auditable annual and interim financial facts with filing anchors.
selected_skills.fallback: Octagon MCP is not configured in this environment; apply the skill's filing structure directly to SEC and issuer primary documents.

selected_skills.name: earnings-capital-allocation
selected_skills.purpose: Separate actual capital spending from management guidance and identify infrastructure investment priorities.
selected_skills.expected_output: Actual-versus-guidance capex trace and investment-priority evidence.
selected_skills.fallback: Octagon MCP is not configured; use official earnings materials and webcast transcripts when published by the issuer.

selected_skills.name: financial-metrics-analysis
selected_skills.purpose: Compare supplier revenue growth and operating-profitability trends on consistent reported periods.
selected_skills.expected_output: Comparable supplier growth and operating-margin panel.
selected_skills.fallback: Calculate directly from primary filings because the skill's preferred MCP is unavailable.

selected_skills.name: finrunbook-tone-review
selected_skills.purpose: Review final English report prose while protecting facts, units, periods, and provenance.
selected_skills.expected_output: Reviewed artifacts and editorial audit log.

selected_skills.name: finrunbook-validator
selected_skills.purpose: Validate provenance, calculations, presentation semantics, and artifact completeness.
selected_skills.expected_output: validation.json and PASS or PASS_WITH_WARNINGS result.

selected_skills.name: writing-clearly-and-concisely
selected_skills.purpose: English-language editor required by the FinRunbook tone-review skill.
selected_skills.expected_output: Concise, neutral report prose with protected facts and provenance unchanged.

steps.description: Define metric dictionary, supplier inclusion rule, and layer-aware relationship model.
Collect hyperscaler capex actuals and guidance from filings and official earnings materials.
Collect supplier relationship evidence and supplier financial/KPI trends.
Build calculations, rankings, and non-additive value-chain analysis.
Generate portable interactive report and structured presentation JSON.
Run tone review, regenerate, validate, and resolve blocking issues.

output_contract.coverage_universe_rule: Four named hyperscalers plus no more than eight public suppliers selected to cover GPU, foundry, memory, networking, power, and cooling; inclusion requires material AI-infrastructure relevance, useful public financial disclosure, and at least one evidenced link into the named-customer ecosystem.
comparison_periods: latest reported interim period available by 2026-09-03
sector_kpis: capex as a share of revenue
supplier backlog or orders where disclosed
output_contract.required_bridge_or_ranking: Rank suppliers by directness of hyperscaler exposure and compare how capex transmits through separate supply-chain layers; explicitly prohibit summing layer revenues as end-market size.

facts.statement: Microsoft cash additions to property and equipment rose from $28.107bn in FY2023 to $64.551bn in FY2025 and $115.948bn in FY2026.
Alphabet purchases of property and equipment rose from $32.251bn in 2023 to $91.447bn in 2025; H1 2026 spending reached $80.598bn.
Amazon net purchases of property and equipment rose from $48.133bn in 2023 to $128.320bn in 2025; TTM spending through Q2 2026 reached $169.007bn.
Meta capex including finance-lease principal rose from $28.103bn in 2023 to $72.215bn in 2025; H1 2026 was $50.918bn and full-year guidance was $130bn-$145bn.
NVIDIA annual revenue and GAAP operating margin expanded sharply across FY2024-FY2026, with Data Center reaching $193.737bn in FY2026.
TSMC revenue, operating margin and HPC-platform revenue rose in every year from 2023 through 2025.
SK hynix swung from a 2023 operating loss to 49% operating margin in 2025 as AI memory and HBM mix rose.
Micron recovered from a FY2023 operating loss to a 26.1% GAAP operating margin in FY2025.
Broadcom revenue rose from $35.819bn in FY2023 to $63.887bn in FY2025; GAAP operating margin dipped after VMware and recovered to 39.9%.
Arista revenue rose from $5.860bn in 2023 to $9.006bn in 2025 while GAAP operating margin held above 38%.
Eaton Electrical Americas sales rose from $10.098bn in 2023 to $13.276bn in 2025; segment margin expanded then eased to 29.9%, while backlog reached $13.246bn.
Vertiv revenue rose from $6.863bn in 2023 to $10.230bn in 2025, with GAAP operating margin expanding to 17.9% and backlog reaching $15.0bn.
Latest supplier indicators remained strong but are not period-comparable across companies.
Microsoft is an evidenced NVIDIA platform customer/adopter.
Alphabet/Google is an evidenced NVIDIA platform customer/adopter.
Amazon/AWS is an evidenced NVIDIA platform customer and co-development partner.
Meta is an evidenced NVIDIA GPU customer/adopter.
Microsoft is an evidenced Arista end customer, accounting for 18% of 2023 and 20% of 2024 Arista revenue.
Meta is an evidenced Arista end customer, accounting for 21% of 2023 and 15% of 2024 Arista revenue.
Alphabet/Google uses Broadcom in its TPU supply chain.
Meta and Broadcom have an evidenced multi-generation MTIA custom-silicon partnership across design, packaging and networking.
Microsoft and Eaton have an evidenced datacenter UPS development and deployment relationship.
TSMC manufactures NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs on a custom 4NP process.
SK hynix supplies and co-develops advanced memory aligned with NVIDIA's AI platform roadmap.
Micron HBM3E is designed into NVIDIA H200 GPUs.
Vertiv collaborates with NVIDIA on GB300 reference designs and provides the surrounding power, cooling and controls framework.
Revenue from suppliers at different layers is not additive: the same deployed system can be reflected in memory, foundry, accelerator, networking and facility-equipment revenue.
facts.reasoning: A single AI server or datacenter deployment contains upstream wafers and memory, downstream accelerators and networking, and surrounding power and cooling equipment. Each supplier can recognize revenue on its own sale, so summing those layer revenues counts portions of the same deployment more than once.
